study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Jing et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Heterogeneous brain dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug-naive patients with major depressive disorder

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To identify subtypes of first-episode drug-naive (FEDN) major depressive disorder (MDD) patients based on brain network characteristics and to investigate their associated neurobiological heterogeneity.

we used the matchIt function in R (https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/MatchIt/ versions/4.4.0/topics/matchit) to select the comparable group from the healthy controls as the healthy-base group for the patients on the following characteristic: sex, age, and educational levels.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Pseudo two sample t-tests were conducted to explore the functional connectivity differences of the ICs between healthy-based controls and subtypes of FEDN-MDD using statistical nonparametric mapping software (SnPM13, http://warwick.ac.uk/snpm; permutation tests n = 5000, age, sex and education as covariates).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two subtypes of FEDN-MDD patients were identified with distinctive abnormal functional network patterns, illness durations, and gray matter abnormalities.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Two patient subtypes were identified with distinctive abnormal functional network patterns, consisting of 10 informative connectivity networks, including the default mode network and frontoparietal network. 16% of patients belonged to subtype I with larger extreme deviations from the normal range and shorter illness duration, while 84% belonged to subtype II with weaker extreme deviations and longer illness duration. Moreover, the structural changes in subtype II patients were more complex than the subtype I patients. Compared with healthy controls, both increased and decreased gray matter (GM) abnormalities were identified in widely distributed brain regions in subtype II patients. In contrast, most abnormalities were decreased GM in subtype I.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The findings provide insight into FEDN depression heterogeneity in biological terms and represent a promising step toward categorical subtype recognition and personalized treatments.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study included treatment-naive patients, so the findings may not apply to MDD groups with multiple prior episodes and active antidepressant therapies. The choice of the k-means clustering algorithm has limitations. The number of ICs was determined empirically. The study was cross-sectional, lacking treatment information. The generalizability is limited due to the small sample size of subtype I.
